newsitem.title: UK: Vassall, former Soviet spy, remembered in London.
newsitem.headline: Vassall, former Soviet spy, remembered in London.

text.p: More than 100 people attended a London memorial service on Thursday for former Soviet spy John Vassall who died two weeks ago.
Vassall, 71, adopted the name John Phillips when he was released from prison in 1972 after serving 10 years in jail for passing secrets to the Soviets between 1956 and 1962.
He died of a suspected heart attack. His death was made public only this week.

"I didn't judge him on his past, but I was very fond of him," Lord Francis Longford, a noted civil libertarian, said at the ceremony in central London. "I admire the way he pulled his life together after what happened to him."
Vassall led a private life after his release from prison and worked as a local archivist in London.
The discovery that Vassall was a spy rocked the Conservative government after his arrest following a stint as a junior naval attache to the British Embassy in Moscow from 1954 to 1956.
A homosexual, Vassall was blackmailed into spying for the Soviets after he was photographed with a male lover while working in the former Soviet Union.
